newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 9.12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 9.12 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 9.12 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 9.23 percent on Friday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 9.66 percent against 10.13 percent on Friday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said the drop in interbank rates were expected after the overnight fell sharply to 7.0/7.5 percent on Friday from 10.0 percent.
Agent banks of Bank Negara Malaysia were seen lending overnight funds on Friday, they said.
"Money is slowly coming back into the system and rates are falling," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
He said trading was thin with few players in the market.
The overnight rate was expected to trade between seven and nine percent, dealers said.
"Some banks are now quite long and this will put some pressure on the overnight," said another dealer.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange extended their rise on the back of softening interbank rates on the cash market.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up three points to 92.44, or an implied yield of 7.56 percent.
The March 1998 contract was up two to 92.75, or 7.25 percent.
